recognize_zh: 一群聚集的大細胞，核為單一、偏心的橢圓形，胞質豐富呈藍紫色、邊緣模糊如彗星狀，且淡染的高基氏區（Golgi zone）與細胞核有距離，這是骨髓抽吸常見的成骨細胞（osteoblasts），不要誤認成漿細胞或轉移癌。
features: Loose cluster of large cells, larger than plasma cells, with ill-defined wispy cytoplasmic borders
Single eccentric oval nucleus often appearing to be extruded toward the cell edge
Fine to lightly stippled chromatin with small indistinct nucleoli
Abundant basophilic, finely granular cytoplasm with a pale Golgi zone set away from the nucleus
Background of red cell aggregates with rouleaux-like stacking and scattered platelets
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (May-Grünwald-Giemsa) shows a loose cluster of large cells with single eccentric oval nuclei, fine chromatin, and abundant basophilic cytoplasm with ill-defined borders. A pale perinuclear-to-central clear zone (Golgi area) is separated from the nucleus in some cells. Nuclear atypia and mitoses are not seen. Findings are consistent with normal osteoblasts, commonly encountered in aspirates from children or areas of active bone remodeling.

ddx.vs: Plasma cells are smaller with clock-face chromatin and a hof immediately adjacent to the nucleus, whereas the osteoblast Golgi zone lies away from the nucleus.
Carcinoma forms cohesive clusters with nuclear pleomorphism, high N:C ratio, prominent nucleoli and molding, unlike the bland, comet-shaped osteoblasts.
Osteoclasts are multinucleated giant cells, while osteoblasts are mononuclear.
